import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure with two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 10))

# Plot 1: Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status
sns.kdeplot(data=df, x='amount', hue='is_fraud', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=axes[0], palette='viridis')
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[0].legend(title='Is Fraud', labels=['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'])

# Plot 2: Fraud Rate by Hour of Day
# Calculate the mean 'is_fraud' for each 'hour_of_day'
fraud_rate_by_hour = df.groupby('hour_of_day')['is_fraud'].mean().reset_index()
sns.barplot(data=fraud_rate_by_hour, x='hour_of_day', y='is_fraud', ax=axes[1], color='skyblue')
axes[1].set_title('Fraud Rate by Hour of Day', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Fraud Rate (Proportion)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_xticks(range(0, 24, 2)) # Set ticks for every 2 hours for clarity

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles/labels
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure with two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 10))

# Plot 1: Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status
sns.kdeplot(data=df, x='amount', hue='is_fraud', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=axes[0], palette='viridis')
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[0].legend(title='Is Fraud', labels=['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'])

# Plot 2: Fraud Rate by Hour of Day
# Calculate the mean 'is_fraud' for each 'hour_of_day'
fraud_rate_by_hour = df.groupby('hour_of_day')['is_fraud'].mean().reset_index()
sns.barplot(data=fraud_rate_by_hour, x='hour_of_day', y='is_fraud', ax=axes[1], color='skyblue')
axes[1].set_title('Fraud Rate by Hour of Day', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Fraud Rate (Proportion)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_xticks(range(0, 24, 2)) # Set ticks for every 2 hours for clarity

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles/labels
plt.tight_layout()
